BURSEVI:v4p165#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p165#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p165#2/r1.claim: The two youths were the king’s cupbearer and baker; they were jailed after a poisoning plot, which the cupbearer abandoned but the baker carried out.
BURSEVI:v4p165#2/r1.anchor: من عبيد الملك الأكبر وهو ريان بن الوليد

BURSEVI:v4p165#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p165#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p165#2/r2.claim: The cupbearer dreamt of three grape clusters, squeezed them into the king’s cup, and served him; wine names the grapes by what they become.
BURSEVI:v4p165#2/r2.anchor: ثلاثة أغصان عليها ثلاثة عناقيد من عنب

BURSEVI:v4p165#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p165#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p165#2/r3.claim: The baker dreamt he carried bread above his head; above means on, as in the command to strike above the necks.
BURSEVI:v4p165#2/r3.anchor: وقال الآخر وهو الخباز إني أريني كأني في مطبخ الملك

BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r1.claim: The baker’s dream had three baskets of bread and foods, with birds of prey eating from the upper basket.
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r1.anchor: فوق رأسي ثلاث سلال فيها خبز وألوان الأطعمة

BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r2.claim: Commentators differ on whether the prisoners truly dreamt or feigned dreams to test Joseph; the rescued cupbearer spoke truth, while the other lied and was crucified.
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r2.anchor: واختلف في أنهما هل رأيا رؤيا أو لم يريا شيئا فتحالما اختبارا ليوسف

BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r3.claim: They asked for interpretations of both dreams and their outcome; plural ‘tell us’ is narrative wording although each man asked separately, like messengers addressed individually.
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r3.anchor: وصيغة المتكلم مع الغير واقعة في الحكاية دون المحكي على طريقة قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r4.claim: Seeing Joseph as good may mean they recognized his skill at dream interpretation, whose readings came true, or that he treated prisoners well and could relieve their distress.
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r4.anchor: يجوز أن تكون من الرؤية بالعين وأن يكون من الرؤية بالقلب

BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r5.claim: Joseph comforted prisoners who had lost hope and suffered long grief, telling them to be glad, patient, and expect reward.
BURSEVI:v4p165#3/r5.anchor: وكان في السجن ناس قد انقطع رجاؤهم وطال حزنهم

QASHANI:12:34-36/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:34-36/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:34-36/r3.claim: The cupbearer represents spiritual love, which discovers in a dream the wine of love pressed from the heart's knowledge while true witnessing is asleep.
QASHANI:12:34-36/r3.anchor: أحدهما قوة المحبة الروحية اللازمة له وهو شرابي الملك الذي يسقيه خمر العشق

QASHANI:12:34-36/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:34-36/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:34-36/r4.claim: The baker represents soul-desire, which sustains the soul; his dream signifies total pursuit of pleasure and appetites, like birds for their swift movement toward gratification.
QASHANI:12:34-36/r4.anchor: والثاني: هوى النفس التي لا تفارقه أيضا بحال

QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r2.claim: Companionship bears fruit even after delay: the cellmate forgot Joseph’s request, but later spoke of him when the king needed a dream interpreted.
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r2.anchor: لصحبة السجن أثر يظهر ولو بعد حين

QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r3.claim: Calling Joseph a beneficent person is a means of approaching him and seeking his beneficence.
QUSHAYRI:v2p77/r3.anchor: ذريعة ، بها يتوسل إلى استجلاب إحسانه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads أعصر عنبا; the standard أعصر خمرا anticipates what the grapes will become, a future state named as though present.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p343/r4.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة ابن مسعود: "إني أراني أعصر عنبا"7

QIRAAT-ER:12:36:8#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:36:8#1/r1.claim: The standard form ends with a short yāʾ.
QIRAAT-ER:12:36:8#1/r1.anchor: Standard form — short yāʾ at end

QIRAAT-ER:12:36:8#2/r1.speaker: author

QIRAAT-ER:12:36:8#2/r1.anchor: Extended yāʾ — both are canonical (7-readers); the iḍāfa/extension variant is a recitational option

QIRAAT-ER:12:36:9#1/r1.speaker: author

QIRAAT-ER:12:36:9#1/r1.anchor: Standard form — short yāʾ at end

QIRAAT-ER:12:36:16#1/r1.claim: The standard form of arānī ends with a short yāʾ.
QIRAAT-ER:12:36:16#1/r1.anchor: Standard form — short yāʾ at end

QIRAAT-ER:12:36:16#2/r1.speaker: author

QIRAAT-ER:12:36:16#2/r1.anchor: Extended yāʾ — both canonical; recitational extension variant

QIRAAT-ER:12:36:19#1/r1.speaker: author

QIRAAT-ER:12:36:24#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:36:24#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:36:24#1/r1.claim: The standard reading retains the hamza in nabbiʾnā.

QIRAAT-ER:12:36:24#2/r1.anchor: Hamza elision — 10-readers variant; same meaning, different phonological shape

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r4.claim: The text elides their imprisonment of Joseph before saying that two young men entered prison with him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r4.anchor: في الكلام حذف تقديره: فسجنوه، فدخل معه السجن غلامان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r5.claim: A report identifies the young men as the king al-Walīd ibn al-Rayyān's baker and cupbearer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r5.anchor: وروي أنهما كانا للملك الأعظم الوليد بن الريان، أحدهما خبازه، والآخر ساقيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r6.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says the king suspected the baker of trying to poison him and the cupbearer of consenting, and jailed both.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r6.anchor: فسجنهما قاله: السدي. ومع تدل على الصحبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r7.claim: The word مع indicates co-presence and a new shared event, so all three were imprisoned at the same time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r7.anchor: ومع تدل على الصحبة واستحداثها، فدل على أنهم سجنوا الثلاثة في ساعة واحدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r8.claim: In prison Joseph comforted the grieving, visited the ill, advocated for the poor, urged goodness, and won the affection of prisoners and the keeper.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r8.anchor: ولما دخل يوسف السجن استمال الناس بحسن حديثه وفضله ونبله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r9.claim: When the keeper offered Joseph his choice of rooms, Joseph said not to love him because love had brought him trials through his aunt, father, and the ʿAzīz's wife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r9.anchor: وقال له: كن في أي البيوت شئت فقال له يوسف: لا تحبني يرحمك الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r10.claim: Joseph told the prisoners that he was skilled at interpreting dreams.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r10.anchor: وكان يوسف عليه السلام قد قال لأهل السجن: إني أعبر الرؤيا وأجيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r11.claim: The two young men said they loved Joseph from their first sight of him; he adjured them not to love him and repeated the trials love had brought.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r11.anchor: وروي أن الفتيين قالا له: إنا لنحبك من حين رأيناك فقال: أنشدكما الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r12.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r12.claim: Qatāda says Joseph encouraged despondent inmates to be patient and hopeful of reward; they praised his character and asked who he was.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p274/r12.anchor: وعن قتادة: كان في السجن ناس قد انقطع رجاؤهم وطال حزنهم، فجعل يقول: اصبروا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r1.claim: Joseph introduces himself as Jacob, God's chosen, son of Isaac, God's sacrificed one, son of Abraham, God's friend; the prison keeper says he would free him if able.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r1.anchor: قال يوسف: ابن صفي الله يعقوب، ابن ذبيح الله إسحاق ابن خليل الله إبراهيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the two men truly saw these dreams and wanted to ask Joseph about them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: رأيا ذلك حقيقة فأرادا سؤاله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود والشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and al-Shaʿbī say the prisoners pretended to dream in order to test Joseph.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r3.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود والشعبي: استعملاها ليجرباه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r4.claim: The cupbearer, called Bunū, describes three grape clusters whose juice he pressed for the king.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r4.anchor: والذي رأى عصر الخمر اسمه بنو قال: رأيت حبلة من كرم لها ثلاثة أغصان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r5.claim: The baker, called Malḥab, describes three baskets of bread carried on his head, from which birds ate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r5.anchor: والذي رأى الخبز اسمه ملحب قال: كنت أرى أن أخرج من مطبخة الملك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r6.claim: The dream verb is like verbs of cognition: its subject and object may be pronouns referring to the same person, though ordinary paired pronouns such as اضربني are disallowed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r6.anchor: ورأى الحلمية جرت مجرى أفعال القلوب في جواز كون فاعلها ومفعولها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r7.claim: Grapes are called wine in anticipation of what they become; some dialects use khamr for grapes directly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r7.anchor: وسمي العنب خمرا باعتبار ما يؤول إليه. وقيل: الخمر بلغة غسان اسم العنب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r8.speaker: المعتمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r8.claim: Al-Muʿtamir recounts asking a Bedouin carrying grapes what he had; the man answered khamr, meaning grapes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r8.anchor: وقال المعتمر: لقيت أعرابيا يحمل عنبا في وعاء فقلت: ما تحمل؟ قال: خمرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r9.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r9.claim: Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read عنبا, but Abū Ḥayyān treats it as an explanatory gloss, since their transmitted mutawātir reading is خمرا and the form conflicts with the codex text.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبي وعبد الله: أعصر عنبا، وينبغي أن يحمل ذلك على التفسير لمخالفته سواد المصحف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows khamr to be described as pressed because pressing is done for its sake.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r10.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويجوز أن يكون وصف الخمر بأنها معصورة، إذ العصر لها ومن أجلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r11.claim: The phrase in ʿAbd Allāh's codex about tharīd is also an explanatory gloss, not a reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r11.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله: فوق رأسي ثريدا تأكل الطير منه، وهو أيضا تفسير لا قراءة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r12.claim: The pronoun in تأويله refers to everything the men related, functioning like a demonstrative meaning that.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r12.anchor: والضمير في تأويله عائد إلى ما قصا عليه، أجري مجرى اسم الإشارة كأنه قيل: بتأويل ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r13.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r13.claim: The majority understand محسنين as skilled in knowledge, since the two men saw that Joseph was learned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r13.anchor: وقال الجمهور: من المحسنين أي في العلم، لأنهما رأيا منه ما علما به أنه عالم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r14.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r14.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Qatāda understand محسنين as kind in speech and courteous to prison inmates.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r14.anchor: وقال الضحاك وقتادة: من المحسنين في حديثه مع أهل السجن وإجماله معهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r15.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r15.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the men meant that Joseph had done them a kindness by interpreting their dreams.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p275/r15.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: أرادا إخباره أنهما يريان له إحسانا عليهما ويدا

TUSTARI:12:36/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:12:36/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:12:36/r1.claim: The two prisoners were called young men because neither outdid the other in making a claim and each referred matters to his companion.
TUSTARI:12:36/r1.anchor: ورجعا في كل ما كان لهما إلى صاحبهما، فسماهما فتيان

FARRA:v2p43/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p43/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p43/r5.claim: المحسنين means learned in knowledge; the author reports Ikrima's two senses of حين: an indefinite period and a fixed six-month period.
FARRA:v2p43/r5.anchor: يقول: من العالمين قد أحسنت العلم. حدثنا الفراء قال: حدثنا ابن الغسيل الأنصاري عن عكرمة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#3/r1.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#3/r1.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī relates that an Arab carrying grapes called them khamr, supporting khamr as a name for grapes before pressing.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#3/r1.anchor: قال الأصمعي: أخبرني المعتمر بن سليمان (2) أنه لقي أعرابيا معه عنب،

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#3/r2.claim: Khamr can mean grapes, or wine itself; Arabic similarly says “I squeezed oil” while meaning olives.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p217#3/r2.anchor: كما يقال: عصرت زيتا؛ وإنما عصرت زيتونا.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p237#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p237#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p237#2/r1.claim: The two young men were servants of the greater king Rayyān ibn al-Walīd: one baker and one cupbearer; an account says they were jailed after a poisoning plot against the king.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p237#2/r1.anchor: غلامان كانا للملك الأكبر الريان بن الوليد : أحدهما خبازه وصاحب طعامه والآخر ساقيه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p237#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p237#2/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ALUSI-FULL:v12p237#2/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the two loved Joseph when they saw him; Joseph begged them not to, since everyone who loved him suffered a trial, but they persisted.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p237#2/r2.anchor: فقد أخرج غير واحد عن ابن إسحق أنهما لما رأياه قالا له

ALUSI-FULL:v12p237#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p237#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p237#2/r3.claim: Calling their imprisonment ‘entering with him’ may suggest it became easier on seeing Joseph; another view says the wording associates Joseph with their prison status and avoids wording that denies his choice. Maʿa ordinarily implies concurrence from the action’s beginning.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p237#2/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن مع تدل على الصحبة والمقارنة لفاعل الفعل في ابتداء تلبسه بالفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r1.claim: For the Queen’s ‘I submitted with Solomon,’ al-Kashf allows ‘with’ to mean submission to God and the Messenger, rather than simultaneous companionship; it suggests she had considered herself religious before her new Islam followed the Prophet’s guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r1.anchor: وقال صاحب الكشف : إنه لا يتعين المحكي عنها المعية الفاعل فجاز أن يراد أسلمت لله ولرسوله مثلا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r2.claim: Some distinguish ongoing Islam from punctual entry, but al-Ālūsī prefers concurrence as the original meaning whenever possible. The object precedes the subject for emphasis; ‘with him’ precedes prison because companionship matters more.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r2.anchor: واختير أن المقارنة هي الأصل ولا يعدل عنها ما أمكنت فتأمل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r3.claim: The sentence follows an implied ‘they imprisoned him’; the two men entered with him. Al-sijn with fatḥa means the prison location, and ‘he said’ answers an implied question.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r3.anchor: كأنه قيل : فلما بدا لهم ذلك سجنوه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r4.claim: The cupbearer’s present-tense dream means he saw himself pressing wine, reportedly from a beautiful vine with three branches; grapes are named for the intended end product. Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd’s ‘grapes’ is gloss, not canonical recitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p238/r4.anchor: وروي أنه قال : رأيت حبلة من كرم حسنة لها ثلاثة أغصان فيها عناقيد عنب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows ‘wine’ to be described as pressed because pressing is done for its sake; the common explanation is metonymy for its outcome. Al-Sijistānī heard reliable eloquent speakers use khamr as masculine.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : يجوز أن يكون وصف الخمر بأنها معصورة لأن العصر من أجلها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r2.claim: Aranī lets subject and object pronouns identify the same person as with verbs of perception: ‘I saw myself pressing wine.’ The baker’s dream has bread, or tharīd in Ibn Masʿūd’s muṣḥaf as a gloss, with birds eating from the upper basket.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r3.claim: ‘Tell us its interpretation’ refers to both visions or what was seen; plural speech can narrate separate requests, as in 23:51. They call Joseph a benefactor for interpreting dreams or for his learning.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r3.anchor: أي أخبرنا بتأويله بتعبيره وما يؤول إليه أمره

ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r4.claim: Qatāda reports that prison inmates were despondent; Joseph urged them to hope and be patient, and they praised his comfort. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says he tended the sick, made room for them, and gathered supplies for the needy.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p239/r4.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم وغيره عن قتادة قال : لما انتهى يوسف إلى السجن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240/r1.claim: The two young men served Egypt’s king al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid ibn Sharwan: one was the baker and the other the cupbearer; the king imprisoned them after a poisoning plot.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240/r1.anchor: ملك مصر الأكبر، أحدهما: خبازه وصاحب طعامه، والآخر: ساقيه وصاحب شرابه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240/r2.claim: A group bribed the two to poison the king; the cupbearer withdrew while the baker accepted. The cupbearer warned the king, survived a test, and the baker’s food killed an animal, so both were jailed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240/r2.anchor: فضمنوا لهذين مالا ليسما الملك في طعامه وشرابه فأجاباهم، ثم إن الساقي نكل عنه، وقبل الخباز الرشوة فسم الطعام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240/r3.claim: Joseph taught dream interpretation in prison; Ibn Masud says the two men invented dreams to test him, while others say they had real dreams that troubled them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240/r3.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: ما رأيا شيئا وإنما تحالما ليجربا يوسف. وقال قوم: بل كانا رأيا حقيقة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r1.claim: The cupbearer’s “wine” means grapes, named for what they become; another view says khamr means grapes in Oman’s language.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r1.anchor: {إني أراني أعصر خمرا} أي: عنبا، سمى العنب خمرا باسم ما يؤول إليه، كما يقال:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r2.claim: The cupbearer saw three grape clusters in a garden and squeezed them into the king’s cup to serve him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r2.anchor: فإذا بأصل حبلة عليها ثلاث عناقيد من عنب فجنيتها، وكان كأس الملك بيدي فعصرتها فيه وسقيت الملك فشربه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r3.claim: The baker saw three baskets above his head containing bread and assorted foods, from which birds of prey ate.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r3.anchor: كأن فوق رأسي ثلاث سلال فيها الخبز وألوان الأطعمة وسباع الطير تنهش منه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r4.claim: Interpreting a dream means explaining what it signifies and how its outcome will unfold; “one of the good” means skilled in interpretation, with ihsan here meaning knowledge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r4.anchor: {نبئنا بتأويله} أخبرنا بتفسيره وتعبيره وما يؤول إليه أمر هذه الرؤيا. {إنا نراك من المحسنين}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r5.claim: Joseph cared for prisoners, visited the ill, made room for them, helped them obtain necessities, and devoted nights to worship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r5.anchor: كان إذا مرض إنسان في السجن عاده وقام عليه، وإذا ضاق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r6.claim: Another account says Joseph comforted the prisoners, introduced his prophetic lineage, and the keeper let him choose his quarters; he asked the two dreamers not to love him because love had repeatedly brought him hardship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r6.anchor: فجعل يسليهم ويقول: أبشروا واصبروا تؤجروا، فيقولون:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r7.claim: Because Joseph knew one prisoner would suffer, he initially avoided their request and instead demonstrated his prophetic sign and called them to monotheism.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p240#2/r7.anchor: فلما قصا عليه الرؤيا كره يوسف أن يعبر لهما ما سألاه لما علم في ذلك من المكروه على أحدهما، فأعرض عن سؤالهما وأخذ في غيره

NAHHAS:v2p329/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p329/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p329/r2.claim: فتيان is dual of فتى; the dream omits 'in sleep'; hamzated نبئنا retains yā' unless hamza is lightened or replaced.
NAHHAS:v2p329/r2.anchor: تثنية فتى وهو من ذوات الياء وقولهم الفتوة شاذ

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r1.claim: Joseph entered prison, where two other men were also admitted: the king's cupbearer and baker, accused of intending to poison him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r1.anchor: أي أدخل يوسف السجن واتفق أنه أدخل حينئذ آخران من عبيد الملك

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r2.claim: The cupbearer says 'I see myself' as a past dream scene; squeezing wine means grapes, called wine in anticipation of what they become.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r2.anchor: { إني أراني } أي في المنام وهي حكاية حال ماضية. { أعصر خمرا } أي عنبا

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r3.claim: The baker's dream shows birds tearing bread carried on his head.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r3.anchor: { وقال الآخر } أي الخباز. { إني أراني أحمل فوق رأسي خبزا تأكل الطير منه }

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r4.claim: They call Joseph one of the good-doers because he interprets dreams well, is learned, speaks to and instructs prisoners, or treats them kindly.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:36/r4.anchor: { نبئنا بتأويله إنا نراك من المحسنين } من الذين يحسنون تأويل الرؤيا، أو من العالمين

BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r1.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r1.claim: Al-Razi says every stage in Joseph's story combined gentleness with hardship, blessing with trial, and eventual relief; harsh coercion can lead to the best outcome with fewer consequences.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r1.anchor: قال الإمام فخر الدين الرازي في كتاب اللوامع : وعلى الجملة فكل أحوال يوسف

BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r2.claim: The prison that appeared to humiliate Joseph instead became a source of honor and showed God's control of events while fulfilling his prior promise.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r3.claim: The two young inmates were the king's baker and cupbearer; the baker suspected that the cupbearer had helped him poison the king.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r3.anchor: فتيان } : خباز الملك وساقيه , ورفع إليه أن الخباز أراد أن يسمه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan says the word مع indicates companionship beginning at that point, so all three entered prison at the same time.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r4.anchor: تدل على الصحبة واستحداثها , فهي تدل على دخول الثلاثة السجن في آن واحد - قاله أبو حيانز

BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r5.claim: Joseph cared for fellow prisoners by comforting the grieving, visiting the sick, advocating for the poor, guiding people to good, and reminding them of God; they felt spiritually blessed by his company.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r5.anchor: يسلي حزينهم , ويعود مريضهم , ويسأل لفقيرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r6.claim: The prisoners and guard praised Joseph's face, character, and speech, and valued the reward, expiation, and purity they learned from him; the guard wished he could release him.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r6.anchor: ما أحسن وجهك وأحسن خلقك وأحسن حديثك ! لقد بورك لنا في جوارك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r7.claim: Joseph asked the two young men not to love him, explaining that love from his aunt, father, and his companion's wife had each preceded a new affliction; they loved him anyway.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r7.anchor: فوالله ما أحبني أحد قط إلا دخل علي من جهته بلاء

BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r8.speaker: الشعبي
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r8.claim: Al-Sha'bi suggests the inmates may have invented the dreams to test Joseph, or perhaps they had seen nothing at all.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r8.anchor: كما قال الشعبي - وإنما صنفا هذا ليختبراه به

BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r9.claim: Their first dream describes a past scene: pressing means extracting liquid, and wine here means grapes destined to become wine.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p37/r9.anchor: والعصر : الاعتماد على ما فيه مائية ليحتلب منه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r1.claim: Carrying is lifting an object with support for transport; bread is prepared food, and birds eating from it completes the second dream.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r2.claim: The inmates ask for interpretation, meaning the outcome to which the dream leads; they infer Joseph can interpret because they see him as excellent in all his affairs.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r2.anchor: أي ما يرجع أمره ويصير إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r3.claim: Joseph seizes their receptiveness to give the most important counsel first: sincere worship of God and rejection of associationism, before answering the dream.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r3.anchor: وهو ما خلق العباد له من الاجتماع على الله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r4.claim: Scholars should give essential counsel when asked a question and may describe their knowledge to help listeners accept it, provided this guides them toward God rather than self-praise.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p38/r4.anchor: فعلى كل ذي علم إذا احتاج إلى سؤاله أحد أن يقدم على جوابه نصحه بما هو الأهم له

DURR-FULL:v4p503/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r8.speaker: يوسف
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r8.claim: On entering prison, Joseph announced that he interprets dreams; the two young men proposed testing him with dreams they had invented rather than actually seen.
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r8.anchor: فلما دخل يوسف عليه السلام السجن قال: إني أعبر الأحلام قال أحد الفتيين: هلم فلنجرب هذا العبد العبراني

DURR-FULL:v4p503/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r9.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r9.claim: The cupbearer dreamed of pressing wine, and the baker of carrying bread from which birds ate.
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r9.anchor: فتراءيا من غير أن يكونا رأيا شيئا ولكنهما خرصا فعبر لهما يوسف خرصهما فقال الساقي: رأيتني أعصر خمرا

DURR-FULL:v4p503/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r10.speaker: يوسف
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r10.claim: Joseph says he can interpret their dreams before their next provision arrives, then predicts the cupbearer will return to service and the baker will be crucified and eaten by birds.
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r10.anchor: لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه في النوم إلا نبأتكما بتأويله في اليقظة ثم قال: {يا صاحبي السجن أما أحدكما

DURR-FULL:v4p503/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r11.speaker: يوسف
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r11.claim: The men deny having dreamed anything, but Joseph says the matter is settled and asks the cupbearer to mention him to his master.
DURR-FULL:v4p503/r11.anchor: ففزعا وقالا: والله ما رأينا شيئا قال يوسف عليه السلام: {قضي الأمر الذي فيه تستفتيان

DURR-FULL:v4p535/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p535/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p535/r1.claim: The two young prisoners were the king's food steward and cupbearer; Qatadah gives the same identification.
DURR-FULL:v4p535/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {ودخل معه السجن فتيان} قال: أحدهما خازن الملك

DURR-FULL:v4p535/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p535/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
DURR-FULL:v4p535/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq names the king's two servants Mujlab and Nabwa; one served wine and the other held another royal duty.
DURR-FULL:v4p535/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن محمد بن إسحق

DURR-FULL:v4p535/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p535/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p535/r3.claim: Joseph warned the two men not to love him because everyone who had loved him had brought him trouble: first his aunt, then his father, then the Aziz's wife; they persisted in their affection.
DURR-FULL:v4p535/r3.anchor: فحدثني عبد الله بن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه أن يوسف عليه الصلاة والسلام قال لهما

DURR-FULL:v4p535/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p535/r4.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v4p535/r4.claim: Mujlab dreamed that birds ate bread carried over his head, while Nabwa dreamed of pressing grapes into wine.
DURR-FULL:v4p535/r4.anchor: وقد كانا رأيا حين ادخلا السجن رؤيا فرأى مجلب أنه رأى فوق رأسه خبزا

DURR-FULL:v4p536/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r2.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r2.claim: Joseph said no one had suffered as he had: his father's love led to his being thrown into a well, and the Aziz's wife's love led to prison.
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r2.anchor: عن عمرو بن دينار قال: قال يوسف عليه السلام: ما لقي أحد في الحب ما لقيت

DURR-FULL:v4p536/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses Joseph's dream of pressing wine as pressing grapes.
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {إني أراني أعصر خمرا} قال: عنبا

DURR-FULL:v4p536/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r4.claim: Ibn Masud recited the phrase as pressing grapes and swore that he received that wording from the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ [اني أراني أعصر عنبا] وقال: والله لقد أخذتها من رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v4p536/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r5.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says khamr here means grapes, which people in Oman call khamr.
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه في قوله {إني أراني أعصر خمرا} يقول: أعصر عنبا

DURR-FULL:v4p536/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses taʾwīlihi as its interpretation or expression.
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {نبئنا بتأويله} قال: عبارته

DURR-FULL:v4p536/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r7.claim: Qatadah says the prisoners admired Joseph's good treatment: he comforted mourners, treated the sick, worshipped diligently, and urged them to endure for reward.
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r7.anchor: وفي قوله {إنا نراك من المحسنين} قال: كان احسانه فيما ذكر لنا أنه كان يعزي

DURR-FULL:v4p536/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r8.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r8.claim: The inmates said Joseph's presence had brought consolation, purification, and hope; he identified his lineage as Joseph son of Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham.
DURR-FULL:v4p536/r8.anchor: فمن أنت يا فتى قال: أنا يوسف ابن صفي الله يعقوب ابن ذبيح الله إسحق

DURR-FULL:v4p538/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p538/r11.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v4p538/r11.claim: The jailer said he would improve Joseph's treatment though unable to release him; Joseph replied that this placed the jailer among the evil and destined him for the Fire's mountains.
DURR-FULL:v4p538/r11.anchor: قال: ذاك من الأخيار وأنت في الأشرار إنما تعد لي جبال أهل النار

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r1.claim: The two prisoners were the king's food keeper and wine server; Qatada also reports this identification.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس في قول الله عز وجل : ودخل معه السجن فتيان احدهما خازن الملك على طعامه ، والاخر ساقي الملك على شرابه

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r2.claim: One prisoner was the king's baker and the other his cupbearer.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ودخل معه السجن فتيان قال : كان احدهما : خباز الملك على طعامه ، والاخر : ساقيه على شرابه

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r3.claim: The king imprisoned the baker for suspected poisoning and the cupbearer because he thought the cupbearer had colluded in the poisoning.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r3.anchor: عن السدي ، قوله : ودخل معه السجن فتيان غضب الملك على خبازه ، بلغه انه سمه فحبسه ، وحبس الساقي

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r4.speaker: ابن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r4.claim: The prisoners served King Rayyan ibn al-Walid; their names were Majlath and Nabū, the latter serving wine. They admired Joseph, who warned that love for him had brought him repeated troubles, but they persisted in admiring his understanding.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2141/r4.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق : ودخل معه السجن فتيان : غلامان كانا للملك الاكبر : الريان ابن الوليد

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r1.claim: Ibn Masud recited “I see myself pressing grapes” in place of “pressing wine.”
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r1.anchor: عن زيد بن وهب قال : قرا عبد الله : اني اراني اعصر عنبا

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r2.claim: “Wine” here means grapes, which people in Oman call wine.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك قال احدهما اني اراني اعصر خمرا فالخمر : العنب ، وانما يسمى اهل عمان العنب : الخمر

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r3.claim: The two prisoners had seen dreams on entering prison: Majlath carried bread eaten by birds, and Nabū pressed wine; they asked Joseph to interpret them.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد وقد كانا رايا حين ادخلا السجن رؤيا فراى مجلث انه يحمل فوق راسه خبزا ياكل الطير منه

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r4.claim: The prisoners had invented their dreams to test Joseph's claim that he interpreted dreams; one said he pressed wine and the other carried bread eaten by birds.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r4.anchor: عن السدي قال : وغضب يعني الملك على خبازه

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r5.speaker: أبو مجلز
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r5.claim: One of the two men who recounted a dream was lying, and the man who was crucified was the liar.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r5.anchor: عن أبي مجلز قال : كان أحد الذين قصا على يوسف الرؤيا كاذبا ، قلت له : فالمصلوب هو الكاذب ؟ قال : نعم

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r6.claim: The prisoners asked Joseph to interpret their dreams because they saw him as a virtuous man, if he would do so.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2142/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد ، قال : فراى مجلث انه يحمل فوق راسه خبزا تاكل الطير منه ، وراى نبو انه يعصر خمرا

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2143/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2143/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2143/r1.claim: Joseph tended sick inmates, made room for the crowded, and sought or collected help for anyone in need.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2143/r1.anchor: عند الضحاك بن مزاحم بخراسان اذ جاءه رجل فساله ، عن قول الله : نبئنا بتاويله

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2143/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2143/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2143/r2.claim: Joseph comforted grieving prisoners and treated the sick; his worship and devotion endeared him to them.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2143/r2.anchor: ثنا قتادة قوله : انا نراك من المحسنين قال : كان احسانه فيما ذكر لنا انه كان يعزى حزينهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r1.claim: All readers use kasra in al-sijn here, meaning the place of confinement, because entering applies to a place, not the act of imprisonment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r1.anchor: هنا بمعنى البيت الذي يسجن فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r2.claim: The two youths were the king's cupbearer and baker, imprisoned after the king became angry; an unnamed report says they were accused of poisoning his food and drink.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r2.anchor: وهذان الفتيان هما ساقي الملك وخبازه غضب عليهما الملك فأمر بسجنهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r3.claim: Dream interpretation was a familiar Egyptian discipline, and God supported Joseph through it among the prisoners.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r3.anchor: وكان تعبير الرؤيا من فنون علمائهم فلذلك أيد الله به يوسف عليه السلام بينهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r4.claim: The youths inferred Joseph's intelligence and assumed he could interpret dreams without having seen proof; “excellent” may mean skilled in interpretation or understanding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r4.anchor: أي المحسنين التعبير ، أو المحسنين الفهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r5.claim: Ihsan here means precision or proficiency, as in saying someone does not “do reading well.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r5.anchor: هو لا يحسن القراءة ، أي لا يتقنها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r6.claim: Prisoners commonly exchanged dreams because they lacked news and conversation, and they hoped dreams would foretell escape.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r6.anchor: لفقدانهم الأخبار التي هي وسائل المحادثة والمحاورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r7.claim: The king's later request shows that Egyptian courtiers included people thought capable of interpreting dreams.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r7.anchor: دل عليه قوله تعالى حكاية عن ملك مصر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r8.claim: Aṣr means squeezing a moist substance to extract liquid; ʿaṣīr names the extracted liquid after its source.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r8.anchor: الضغط باليد أو بحجر أو نحوه على شيء فيه رطوبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r9.claim: Bread is a baked portion of flour and water, also called a loaf; “its interpretation” refers either to the mentioned matter or to the dream as a class.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p268#2/r9.anchor: اسم لقطعة من دقيق البر أو الشعير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r6.claim: The two prisoners entered with Joseph either at the same time or separately; مع does not settle the timing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r6.anchor: تحتمل أن تكون باقتران وقت الدخول، وأن لا تكون بل دخلوا أفذاذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r7.claim: The two young men reportedly served the great king al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan: one was his baker and the other his cupbearer.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r8.claim: Fatā means a young man, but can also refer to an enslaved person or a free servant; the two may fit all these senses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r8.anchor: قد تقع اللفظة على المملوك وعلى الخادم الحر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r9.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r9.claim: Al-Suddi says the king suspected the baker of trying to poison him and imprisoned both men because the cupbearer agreed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r9.anchor: الخابز منهما أراد سمه، ووافقه على ذلك الساقي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r10.claim: Joseph won the prisoners’ affection through his speech and virtue, comforting the sad, visiting the ill, helping the poor, and urging good.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r10.anchor: وكان يسلي حزينهم ويعود مريضهم ويسأل لفقيرهم ويندبهم إلى الخير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r11.claim: When the prison keeper offered Joseph his choice of rooms, Joseph asked him not to love him, recalling the harm that followed his aunt’s, father’s, and the governor’s wife’s affection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r11.anchor: لا تحبني يرحمك الله، فلقد أدخلت علي المحبة مضرات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r12.claim: Ibn Masud says the two prisoners staged the dreams to test Joseph’s interpretation skill.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r12.anchor: فروي عن ابن مسعود أن الفتيين استعملا هاتين المنامتين ليجرباه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r13.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r13.claim: Mujahid says the two prisoners really saw the dreams and wanted to ask Joseph about them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r13.anchor: عم مجاهد أنهما رأيا ذلك حقيقة، فأرادا سؤاله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r14.claim: One prisoner, reportedly named Banu, dreamed of a vine with three branches and bunches of grapes that he pressed for the king.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r15.claim: The other, reportedly named Majlath, dreamed he carried three baskets of bread on his head as birds ate from the top.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243/r15.anchor: وعلى رأسي ثلاث سلال فيها خبز، والطير تأكل من أعلاه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r1.claim: Some say the grape is called wine by what it will become; others say this is the language of Oman’s Azd.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r1.anchor: قيل: إنه سمى العنب خمرا بالمئال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r2.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r2.claim: Al-Asmaʿi recounts an Arab carrying grapes who answered that he was carrying wine, meaning grapes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r2.anchor: ما تحمل؟ قال: خمرا، أراد العنب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r3.claim: Ubay ibn Kaʿb and Ibn Masud read the dream as pressing grapes rather than wine.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r3.anchor: في قراءة أبي بن كعب وعبد الله بن مسعود «إني أراني أعصر عنبا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, the phrase can describe wine as pressed, since pressing is done for its sake.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r5.claim: The bread may have been tharīd; Ibn Masud’s codex explicitly says tharīd above the dreamer’s head.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r5.anchor: فوق رأسي ثريدا تأكل الطير منه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r6.claim: The majority understand the prisoners’ praise to mean that Joseph was excellent in knowledge.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak and Qatada understand the praise as Joseph’s kind conduct and good treatment of fellow prisoners.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r7.anchor: من المحسنين في جريه مع أهل السجن وإجماله معهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r8.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p243#2/r8.claim: Ibn Ishaq says they meant Joseph had done them a personal kindness by interpreting their dreams.

SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r1.claim: قال أحدهما is an independent clause, not a circumstantial one: they did not say this while entering, and entry cannot become a dream; إني is the object of قال.
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { قال أحدهما }: مستأنف لا محل له، ولا يجوز أن يكون حالا

SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r2.claim: Some treat dream أراني like a verb of knowledge taking two objects, with أعصر as the second; others take أعصر as a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r2.anchor: و " أراني " هنا متعدية لمفعولين عند بعضهم إجراء للحلمية مجرى العلمية

SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r3.claim: Dream cognition allows subject and object pronouns to refer to the same person, as here; ordinary verbs instead require an explicit reflexive or separate object.
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r3.anchor: وجرت الحلمية مجرى العلمية أيضا في اتحاد فاعلها ومفعولها ضميرين متصلين

SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r4.claim: When the causative hamza is added to this dream verb, it takes a third object, as in the cited construction in al-Anfal 8:43.
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r4.anchor: وإذا دخلت همزة النقل على هذه الحلمية تعدت لثالث، وقد تقدم هذا في قوله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r5.claim: خمر means grapes metaphorically because grapes become wine; others say it literally meant grapes in Ghassan and Azd Oman speech.
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r5.anchor: والخمر: العنب أطلق عليه ذلك مجازا، لأنه آيل إليه كما يطلق الشيء على الشيء

SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r6.speaker: المعتمر
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r6.claim: Al-Muʿtamir recounts an Arab carrying grapes who called them wine.
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r6.anchor: وقيل: بل الخمر: العنب حقيقة في لغة غسان وأزد عمان.

SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r7.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r7.claim: Their explanatory reading أعصر عنبا does not establish synonymy or a recited variant; it is glossing, like Abdullah's explanatory ثريدا.
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r7.anchor: وعن المعتمر: " لقيت أعرابيا حاملا عنبا في وعاء فقلت: ما تحمل؟ فقال: خمرا.

SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r8.claim: تأكل الطير describes خبزا; فوق may modify carrying or be a circumstantial phrase from خبزا.
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r8.anchor: و " تأكل الطير " صفة لخبزا. و " فوق " يجوز أن يكون ظرفا للحمل

SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r9.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r9.claim: Al-Shaykh and al-Zamakhshari take its pronoun in بتأويله as referring to what the two men recounted, like a demonstrative phrase; another view says each means his own dream.
SAMIN-DURR:12:36/r9.anchor: قال الشيخ: " عائد على ما قصا عليه، أجري مجرى اسم الإشارة كأنه قيل بتأويل ذلك "

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r1.claim: The mention of the two youths entering prison implies that Joseph himself had been imprisoned, though this was not stated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج فيه دليل على أنه حبس وإن لم يذكر ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r2.claim: The two “youths” may have been young or old, since an enslaved man could be called a fatā at any age; Ibn al-Anbari ties the label to their being owned.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r2.anchor: فتيان جائز أن يكونا حدثين أو شيخين لأنهم يسمون المملوك فتى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r3.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r3.claim: The king of Egypt was poisoned against by his baker and cupbearer, who were imprisoned; Joseph offered to interpret dreams, and one proposed testing him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r3.anchor: عمر ملك مصر فملوه فدسوا إلى خبازه وصاحب شرابه أن يسماه فبلغه ذلك فحبسهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود والسدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r4.claim: Ibn Masud and al-Suddi say the two prisoners invented their dreams to test Joseph.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r4.anchor: أحدها أنها كانت كذبا وإنما سألاه تجريبا قاله ابن مسعود والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r5.speaker: مجاهد وابن إسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r5.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Ishaq say both dreams were true.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r5.anchor: والثاني أنها كانت صدقا قاله مجاهد وابن إسحاق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r6.speaker: أبو مجلز
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r6.claim: Abu Mujliz says only the man who was crucified lied; the other prisoner's dream was true.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p222/r6.anchor: والثالث أن الذي صلب منهما كان كاذبا وكان الآخر صادقا قاله أبو مجلز

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r1.claim: The cupbearer says he saw himself pressing grapes; the verse calls the grapes wine.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ( قال أحدهما ) يعني الساقي ( إني أراني ) أي في النوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين وابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r2.claim: Most commentators say grapes are named for the wine they become; Ibn al-Anbari notes Arabic can name the source by its eventual product.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r2.anchor: أحدها أنه سماه باسم ما يؤول إليه لأن المعنى لا يلتبس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r3.speaker: الضحاك والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Zajjaj say “wine” means grapes in the language of Oman; Ibn al-Qasim adds that Quraysh knew this usage.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r3.anchor: والثاني أن الخمر في لغة أهل عمان اسم للعنب قاله الضحاك والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r4.claim: A third explanation supplies an omitted noun: he presses wine grapes or grapes intended for wine.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r4.anchor: والثالث أن المعنى أعصر عنب خمر وأصل خمر وسبب خمر فحذف المضاف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r5.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas's report gives the dreams as three grape clusters squeezed into a cup for the king and three bread baskets, from the top of which a bird ate.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r5.anchor: رأى يوسف ذات يوم الخباز والساقي مهمومين فقال ما شأنكما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r6.claim: “Tell us its interpretation” means tell us what the dream signifies.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r7.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r7.claim: Mujahid transmits that “one of the doers of good” means Joseph cared for the sick, treated them, and comforted the grieving.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r7.anchor: أنه كان يعود المرضى ويداويهم ويعزي الحزين رواه مجاهد عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r8.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r8.claim: Ibn Ishaq interprets their praise as a promise that Joseph is kind if he explains the dream.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r8.anchor: إنا نراك محسنا إن أنبأتنا بتأويله قاله ابن إسحاق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r9.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r9.claim: Al-Farra reads “doers of good” as learned people with excellent knowledge; Ibn al-Anbari says the object is omitted, since Joseph had taught them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r9.anchor: إنا نراك من العالمين قد أحسنت العلم قاله الفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj says they mean that Joseph is skilled at interpretation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r10.anchor: والرابع إنا نراك ممن يحسن التأويل ذكره الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r11.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r11.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says they praise Joseph for doing good to himself by adhering to obedience to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p223/r11.anchor: إنا نراك محسنا إلى نفسك بلزومك طاعة الله ذكره ابن الأنباري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r1.claim: Qatada identifies the two prisoners as the king's cupbearer and baker.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: كان أحدهما ساقي الملك، والآخر خبازه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq names the wine official Nabwa and the baker Majlath.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r2.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: كان اسم الذي على الشراب "نبوا"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the king jailed them because he suspected they had conspired to poison his food and drink.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r3.anchor: قال السدي: وكان سبب حبس الملك إياهما أنه توهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r4.claim: Yusuf was known in prison for generosity, trustworthiness, truthful speech, worship, dream interpretation, kindness to prisoners, visiting the sick, and meeting their needs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r4.anchor: يوسف، عليه السلام، قد اشتهر في السجن بالجود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r5.claim: The two men loved Yusuf; he replied that affection had previously brought him harm through his aunt, father, and the Aziz's wife.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r5.anchor: إنه ما أحبني أحد إلا دخل علي من محبته ضرر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r6.claim: Ibn Masud recited the cupbearer's dream as squeezing grapes rather than wine; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits this reading from him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود: أنه قرأها: "أعصر عنبا"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak explains wine here as grapes and says Omanis call grapes wine.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r7.anchor: وقال الضحاك في قوله: {إني أراني أعصر خمرا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r8.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r8.claim: Ikrima gives the cupbearer's dream as planting a grapevine, squeezing its clusters, and serving the king; Yusuf said he would leave prison after three days and serve him wine.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r8.anchor: وقال عكرمة: رأيت (3) فيما يرى النائم أني غرست حبلة من عنب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r9.claim: The majority view is that both prisoners truly dreamed and requested Yusuf's interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r9.anchor: والمشهور عند الأكثرين ما ذكرناه، وأنهما رأيا مناما وطلبا تعبيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r10.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r10.claim: A report cited by Ibn Jarir says the prisoners had no dreams and only pretended in order to test Yusuf.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p387#2/r10.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: ما رأى صاحبا يوسف شيئا

JISHUMI:v5p3641/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r9.claim: ʿAṣr is pressing something to extract what it contains; clouds are called muʿṣirāt because rain is pressed from them, and a people who receive rain are said to have entered a rainy state.
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r9.anchor: العصر: مصدر عصر يعصر عصرا، وهو الاعتماد على الشيء ليستجلب ما فيه

JISHUMI:v5p3641/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r10.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r10.claim: Al-Zajjāj says fityān could mean young men or enslaved servants, whether old or young; a male servant is fatā and a female servant fatāt.
JISHUMI:v5p3641/r10.anchor: قال الزجاج: كانوا يسمون المملوك فتى، شيخا كان أو شابا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r1.claim: Maʿa marks companionship being newly entered into, so the two youths entered prison in Yusuf's company.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r1.anchor: يدل على معنى الصحبة واستحداثها ، تقول : خرجت مع الأمير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r2.claim: The youths were the king's baker and cupbearer, imprisoned on suspicion that they were poisoning him when Yusuf was admitted.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r2.anchor: { فتيان } عبدان للملك : خبازه وشرابيه : رقي إليه أنهما يسمانه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r3.claim: Their statements describe past dreams; khamr names grapes by what they become, and in the language of Oman it means grapes directly.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r3.anchor: { إنى أرانى } يعني في المنام ، وهي حكاية حال ماضية { أعصر خمرا } يعني عنبا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads ʿinaban, grapes, in place of khamran.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r4.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود ( أعصر عنبا )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r5.claim: Muḥsinīn may mean skilled interpreters of dreams, learned men, or people who treat fellow prisoners well.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r5.anchor: { من المحسنين } من الذين يحسنون عبارة الرؤيا ، أي : يجيدونها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r6.claim: Qatāda reports that Yusuf comforted despondent prisoners, urging them to be patient and promising reward; they praised his character and asked who he was.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r6.anchor: وعن قتادة : كان في السجن ناس قد انقطع رجاؤهم وطال حزنهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r7.claim: A prison report says Yusuf identified himself through his lineage: son of Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham, and the guard promised him good treatment despite being unable to free him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r7.anchor: أنا يوسف ابن صفي الله يعقوب ابن ذبيح الله إسحاق ابن خليل الله إبراهيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r8.claim: Yusuf asked the two men not to love him, saying that love had brought him calamity through his aunt, father, and the Aziz's wife.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r8.anchor: أنشدكما بالله أن لا تحباني ، فوالله ما أحبني أحد قط إلا دخل علي من حبه بلاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r9.speaker: الشعبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r9.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says the two men feigned dreams to test Yusuf: the cupbearer dreamed of three grape clusters pressed for the king, while the baker dreamed of three food baskets attacked by birds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r9.anchor: وعن الشعبي أنهما تحالما له ليمتحناه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r10.claim: The pronoun in nabbiʾnā bi-taʾwīlihi refers to the story they recounted and functions like a demonstrative pronoun.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p441#2/r10.anchor: والضمير يجري مجرى اسم الإشارة في نحوه كأنه قيل : نبئنا بتأويل ذلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says one prisoner was the king's food steward and the other his cupbearer; the king, al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan, suspected them of poisoning him and imprisoned them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r2.claim: Mujahid says the prisoners told Joseph they loved him; Joseph asked them not to love him because the love of his aunt, father, and al-Aziz's wife had brought him tribulation, and he wanted love only from his Lord.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r3.claim: They are called fatayan because each was a slave, and slave may mean a young man regardless of age.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r4.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Ishaq say the prisoners had true dreams and Joseph's interpretations came true; Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophetic maxim that the truest dreams belong to the most truthful speakers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r4.anchor: أنها كانت رؤيا صدق رأياها وسألاه عنها قال مجاهد وابن إسحاق

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r5.claim: Through Muhammad ibn Sirin, Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying the most truthful dreams belong to the most truthful speakers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r6.claim: Ibn Masud and al-Suddi say the prisoners invented dreams to test Joseph, then claimed they were joking after his answer; he replied that the matter they asked about had been decided.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r7.speaker: أبو مجلز
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r7.claim: Abu Mijlaz says one prisoner, the one who was crucified, had lied in his dream, while the other had spoken truthfully.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r8.claim: Yakhmur here means grapes, either named for what their juice becomes or because Omanis call grapes khamr; Ibn Masud read anaba, grapes.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r9.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says people of Oman call grapes khamr; Ibn Masud read the phrase as 'I see myself pressing grapes.'

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r10.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says the prisoners called Joseph a benefactor because he visited their sick, consoled the grieving, and made room for cramped inmates.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r10.anchor: لأنه كان يعود مريضهم ويعزي حزينهم ويوسع على من ضاق مكانه منهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r11.claim: Other explanations say Joseph encouraged patience and promised reward, was skilled in knowledge, accepted excuses, or put others' rights before his own.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r11.anchor: معناه لأنه كان يأمرهم بالصبر ويعدهم بالثواب والأجر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r12.speaker: ابن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p35/r12.claim: Ibn Ishaq says they called Joseph a benefactor in the hope that he would interpret their dreams for them.

MUJAHID:v1p316/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p316/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p316/r1.claim: Mujahid says the prisoners asked Joseph to interpret what they had seen; after he interpreted it, they said they had not really dreamed and had only been playing, but Joseph replied that the matter he was asked about had already come to pass as interpreted.
MUJAHID:v1p316/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ نبئنا بتأويله ﴾ يعني تأويل ما رأينا فلما عبر لهما قالا ما رأينا رؤيا

MUQATIL:12:36/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:36/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:36/r1.claim: The baker and cupbearer entered prison after reports that each planned to poison the king's food or drink; their names were Sharham Aqam and Sharham Asham.
MUQATIL:12:36/r1.anchor: ورقي إلى الملك أن غلامه الخباز يريد أن يجعل في طعامه سما، ورقي إليه في غلامه الساقي مثل ذلك، فذلك قوله: { ودخل معه السجن فتيان }

MUQATIL:12:36/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:36/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:36/r2.claim: The cupbearer dreamed of three grape clusters that he pressed and served to the king; khamr here means grapes.
MUQATIL:12:36/r2.anchor: { قال أحدهمآ إني أراني } في المنام كأني { أعصر خمرا } ، يعني عنبا،

MUQATIL:12:36/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:36/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:36/r3.claim: The baker dreamed of three baskets topped by a dish of bread; Muqatil cites 8:12 and 14:26 for “above” meaning the uppermost part.
MUQATIL:12:36/r3.anchor: { وقال الآخر إني أراني } ، رأيت في المنام كأني { أحمل فوق رأسي خبزا } ، ثلاث سلال، وأعلاهن جفنة من خبز فوق رأسي،

MUQATIL:12:36/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:36/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:36/r4.claim: Joseph's kindness in prison included visiting and treating the sick, consoling the distressed, and worshipping God.
MUQATIL:12:36/r4.anchor: وكان إحسانه في السجن أنه كان يعود مرضاهم ويداويهم، ويعزي مكروبهم، ورآه متعبدا لربه، فهذا إحسانه.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r1.claim: The two young men were the king's enslaved baker and cupbearer, imprisoned on a poisoning accusation at the same time as Joseph; maʿa requires their entry to be in his company.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r1.anchor: عبدان للملك خبازه وشرابيه بتهمة السم فادخلا السجن ساعة ادخل يوسف

NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r2.claim: The cupbearer sees himself pressing grapes for wine; grapes are named for their outcome, or khamr is the Omani word for grapes.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r2.anchor: أى عنبا تسمية للعنب بما يؤول إليه أو الخمر بلغته عمان اسم للعنب

NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r3.claim: The baker sees himself carrying bread over his head for birds to eat; they ask Joseph to interpret both dreams.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r3.anchor: فإنك تداوى المريض وتعزى الحزين وتسوع على الفقير

NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r4.claim: Their praise means either that Joseph interprets dreams well or that he cares for prisoners by treating the ill, comforting the sad, and helping the poor.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r4.anchor: من الذين يحسنون عبارة الرؤيا أو من المحسنين إلى أهل السجن

NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r5.claim: Another account says the pair conspired to test Joseph: the cupbearer dreamed of three grape clusters from a vine and serving the king; the baker dreamed of three food baskets eaten by birds.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p188#2/r5.anchor: وقيل أنهما تحالماله يمتحناه فقال الشرابى إنى رأيت كأنى فى بستان

ZAJJAJ:v3p108/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p108/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p108/r6.claim: The phrase ‘entered the prison’ already shows that Joseph was imprisoned; fityān can be young men or elders, because slaves were called fatā.
ZAJJAJ:v3p108/r6.anchor: ولم يقل فحبس لأن في قوله: (ودخل معه السجن) دليلا أنه حبس

ZAJJAJ:v3p108/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p108/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p108/r7.claim: The dreamer need not say ‘in sleep’: the circumstances show that he does not see himself pressing grapes while awake. In Omani usage khamr can mean grapes, though it may also mean wine itself.
ZAJJAJ:v3p108/r7.anchor: ولم يقل إني أراني في النوم أعصر خمرا، لأن الحال

ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r1.claim: ‘I press wine’ means pressing grapes that will become wine; similarly, a thing may be named by its eventual product.
ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r1.anchor: أي أعصر عنب الخمر أي العنب الذي يكون عصيره خمرا

ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r2.claim: ‘Tell us its interpretation’ refers to what they dreamed, proving this was a dream, since a waking sight needs no interpretation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r2.anchor: وقولهما (نبئنا بتأويله) يدل على أنهما رأيا ذلك

ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r3.speaker: قالوا
ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r3.claim: ‘One of the beneficent’ is explained as helping the wronged, supporting the weak, and visiting the sick; another explanation is that Joseph interpreted dreams well.
ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r3.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنه كان يعين المظلوم وينصر الضعيف،

ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r4.claim: The verse supports the reality of true dreams; denying that any dream can be true rejects Qur’an and the Prophet’s report that a dream is one-fortieth of prophecy, since both prophets and truthful dreams disclose the future.
ZAJJAJ:v3p109/r4.anchor: وهذا دليل أن أمر الرؤيا صحيح، وأنها لم تزل في الأمم الخالية

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r1.claim: Fityan is the dual of fata, a weak-y verb; the form al-futu is irregular.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r1.anchor: فتيان» تثنية فتى وهو من ذوات الياء، وقولهم: الفتو شاذ

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r2.speaker: وهب وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r2.claim: Wahb and others say Joseph was paraded in chains on a donkey as punishment for disobeying his mistress; he said that was easier than Hell's punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r2.anchor: قال وهب وغيره: حمل يوسف إلى السجن مقيدا على حمار، وطيف به «هذا جزاء من

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r3.claim: When Joseph reached the prison, its hopeless inmates heard him urge patience and promise of reward; they praised his speech and asked who he was.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r3.anchor: فلما انتهى يوسف إلى السجن وجد فيه قوما قد انقطع رجاؤهم، واشتد بلاؤهم فجعل يقول

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Joseph comforted the grieving, visited and treated the sick and wounded, prayed and wept until the prison seemed to weep, and became beloved to inmates and jailer.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لما قالت المرأة لزوجها إن هذا العبد العبراني قد فضحني، وأنا أريد

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r5.claim: When the jailer said he loved Joseph, Joseph warned him that his father's love had led his brothers to harm him and his mistress's love had led to prison.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r5.anchor: له: يا يوسف! لقد أحببتك حبا لم أحب شيئا حبك فقال: أعوذ بالله من حبك

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r6.claim: The king's baker and cupbearer were plotted against to poison the king; the baker agreed, the cupbearer refused and alerted the king, and both were jailed.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r6.anchor: فدسوا إلى خبازه وصاحب شرابه أن يسماه جميعا، فأجاب الخباز

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r7.claim: An alternative says the baker put poison in food while the cupbearer warned the king not to eat; the baker warned him not to drink, but a test showed the food was poisoned. They spent a year in prison with Joseph.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r7.anchor: وقد قيل: إن الخباز وضع السم في الطعام، فلما حضر الطعام قال الساقي: أيها الملك

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r8.speaker: الثعلبي عن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r8.claim: Al-Tha'labi, citing Ka'b, names the cupbearer Manja and the baker Majlath.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r8.anchor: واسم الساقي منجا، والآخر مجلث ذكره الثعلبي عن كعب

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r9.speaker: النقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r9.claim: Al-Naqqash gives different names for the two men: Sharham and Sarham.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r9.anchor: وقال النقاش: اسم أحدهما شرهم، والآخر سرهم الأول بالشين المعجمة، والآخر بالسين المهملة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r10.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r10.claim: Al-Tabari says the man who dreamed of pressing grapes was Nabu; al-Suhayli mentions the other's name but says he did not retain it.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r10.anchor: وقال الطبري: الذي رأى أنه يعصر خمرا هو نبو، قال السهيلي: وذكر اسم الآخر ولم

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r11.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r11.claim: Al-Mawardi says they are called fityan because they were slaves, since a slave is called fata whether young or old.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r11.anchor: وقال «فتيان» لأنهما كانا عبدين، والعبد يسمى فتى، صغيرا كان أو كبيرا ذكره الماوردي

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r12.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r12.claim: Al-Qushayri says fata may be a customary word for slave, while another possibility is that it means a servant, whether or not enslaved.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r12.anchor: وقال القشيري: ولعل الفتى كان اسما للعبد في عرفهم ولهذا قال: «تراود فتاها عن نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r13.claim: The two men may have entered prison before, after, or at the same time as Joseph; the verse only requires that they entered the same room with him.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36/r13.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون حبسهما مع حبس يوسف أو بعده أو قبله، غير أنهما دخلا معه

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r1.claim: Joseph explained that pressing wine meant pressing grapes; Ibn Masud's reading makes the word grapes explicit.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r1.anchor: إني أراني أعصر خمرا» أي عنبا كان يوسف قال لأهل السجن: إني أعبر الأحلام

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says the two men asked Joseph to test him despite having seen no dreams.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r2.anchor: فسألاه من غير أن يكونا رأيا شيئا قاله ابن مسعود

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r3.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r3.claim: Al-Tabari says the men first asked Joseph about his knowledge; after he offered to interpret dreams, they asked about their visions.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r3.anchor: وحكى الطبري أنهما سألاه عن علمه فقال: إني أعبر الرؤيا فسألاه عن رؤياهما

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say the dreams were true visions, which is why their interpretations came true.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r4.anchor: ابن عباس ومجاهد: كانت رؤيا صدق رأياها وسألاه عنها ولذلك صدق تأويلها

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r5.claim: A Sahih report from Abu Hurayra says the most truthful of you in speech have the truest dreams.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r5.anchor: وفي الصحيح عن أبي هريرة عن النبي

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r6.claim: Another view says they fabricated dreams to test Joseph; Ibn Masud and al-Suddi hold this.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r6.anchor: وقيل: إنها كانت رؤيا كذب سألاه عنها تجريبا وهذا قول ابن مسعود والسدي

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r7.speaker: أبو مجلز
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r7.claim: Abu Mijlaz says the man who was crucified lied about his dream while the other told the truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن المصلوب منهما كان كاذبا، والآخر صادقا قاله أبو مجلز

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r8.claim: From Ibn Abbas, al-Tirmidhi transmits that a person who lies about a dream will be made to tie two barley grains together on Judgment Day, which he cannot do; al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r8.anchor: من تحلم كاذبا كلف يوم القيامة أن يعقد بين شعيرتين

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r9.claim: A report from Ali says a dream liar will be tasked on Judgment Day to tie a grain; al-Tirmidhi calls it hasan.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r9.anchor:
قال:
" من كذب في حلمه كلف يوم القيامة عقد شعيرة "
قال: حديث حسن

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that the men awoke troubled, told Joseph about their disturbing dreams, and asked him to interpret them; the account indicates actual dreams.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما رأيا رؤياهما أصبحا مكروبين فقال لهما يوسف: مالي أراكما مكروبين
