QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r11.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak says Joseph's kindness meant tending sick prisoners, making room for cramped inmates, and gathering help for the needy.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r11.anchor: قال الضحاك: كان إذا مرض الرجل من أهل السجن قام به، وإذا ضاق وسع له

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r12.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r12.claim: Al-Farra says محسنين can mean people who are accomplished in knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r12.anchor: وقيل: «من المحسنين» أي العالمين الذين أحسنوا العلم، قاله الفراء

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r13.speaker: ابن إسحق
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r13.claim: Ibn Ishaq takes من المحسنين to mean that Joseph had treated them well if he interpreted their dreams.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r13.anchor: وقال ابن إسحق: «من المحسنين» لنا إن فسرته، كما يقول: افعل كذا وأنت محسن

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r14.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r14.claim: Al-Dahhak says خمر can mean grapes in the dialect of Oman; Ibn Masud reads عنبا, and al-Asma'i reports a Bedouin calling grapes khamr.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r14.anchor: فذلك قوله: «إني أراني أعصر خمرا» أي عنبا، بلغة عمان، قاله الضحاك. وقرأ ابن مسعود

QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r15.claim: Another grammatical explanation supplies an omitted إضافة, meaning grapes for wine; the forms خمرة، خمر، خمور follow the pattern of date/date-palm plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:36-37/r15.anchor: وقيل: معنى. «أعصر خمرا» أي عنب خمر، فحذف المضاف. ويقال: خمرة وخمر وخمور

RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r5.claim: The text omits that Joseph was imprisoned; the next clause implies it. The two young men were the king's food and drink servants, jailed over a suspected poisoning plot.
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r5.anchor: لما أرادوا حبسه حبسوه وحذف ذلك لدلالة قوله

RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r6.claim: He suggests the youths may have told Joseph of their sadness and dreams, or may have seen him demonstrate knowledge of dream interpretation before asking him.
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r6.anchor: لعله عليه السلام سألهما عن حزنهما وغمهما فذكرا إنا رأينا في المنام هذه الرؤيا

RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r7.claim: Joseph could infer that they served the king from their use of rabb for their master in the later statements about serving wine and asking to be remembered.
RAZI-FULL:v18p107/r7.anchor: هما غلامان كانا للملك الأكبر بمصر أحدهما صاحب طعامه

RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r1.claim: Their visions matched their professions: one pressed grapes for wine, while the other carried bread for birds to eat.
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r1.anchor: رؤيا كل واحد منهما تناسب حرفته لأن أحدهما رأى أنه يعصر الخمر والآخر كأنه يحمل فوق رأسه خبزا

RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says the two men had seen nothing and invented dreams to test Joseph's interpretive skill.
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : ما كانا رأيا شيئا

RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says they really dreamed upon entering prison: the cupbearer saw three vine branches, pressed their grapes into the king's cup, and served him.
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد كانا قد رأيا حين دخلا السجن رؤيا

RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r4.claim: In Mujahid's account, the baker saw three baskets of varied bread on his head while predatory birds tore from them.
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r4.anchor: وإذا سباع الطير تنهش منه فذلك قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r5.claim: The wording أرىني and their request for its interpretation show that they were describing dreams; otherwise saying I press wine would suffice.
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r5.anchor: أنه لو لم يقصد النوم كان ذكر قوله

RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r6.claim: He offers three explanations for pressing wine: omitted grapes, naming something by its eventual product, or calling grapes wine in Omani usage.
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r6.anchor: أي العنب الذي يكون عصيره خمرا فحذف المضاف

RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r7.speaker: أبو صالح
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r7.claim: Abu Salih says people in Oman call grapes khamr; al-Dahhak adds that the Quran came in the tongues of all Arab groups.
RAZI-FULL:v18p107#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو صالح : أهل عمان يسمون العنب بالخمر

RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r1.claim: Taʾwīl is what a thing ultimately returns to, the endpoint toward which the matter leads.
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r1.anchor: تأويل الشيء ما يرجع إليه وهو الذي يؤل إليه آخر ذلك الأمر

RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r2.claim: He explains the youths' praise as Joseph's kindness and fine conduct, care for sick and sorrowful prisoners, or devotion in fasting and prayer, which made him trustworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r2.anchor: معناه إنا نراك تؤثر الإحسان وتأتي بمكارم الأخلاق وجميع الأفعال الحميدة

RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that they praised Joseph's exceptional skill at interpreting dreams, citing his later statement about being taught interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r3.anchor: وذلك لأنه متى عبر لم يخط

RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r4.claim: He argues dream interpretation is real: during sleep the rational soul is less occupied with the body and can encounter higher realities, whose traces appear as images that an interpreter deciphers.
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r4.anchor: وفي وقت النوم يقل هذا التشاغل فتقوى على هذه المطالعة فإذا وقعت الروح

RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r5.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r5.claim: A report from the Prophet classifies dreams as self-talk, satanic dreams, and true dreams; al-Razi calls this a sound division in rational inquiry.
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r5.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r6.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r6.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that a righteous person's dream is one forty-sixth of prophecy.
RAZI-FULL:v18p108/r6.anchor: وقال عليه السلام : ( رؤيا الرجل الصالح جزء من ستة وأربعين جزءا من النبوة )

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

ASAD-NOTES:12:36#n35/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:36#n35/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:36#n35/r1.claim: The two prisoners were the King's cup-bearer and baker, according to the Bible, which the Qur'an does not contradict; their offences are unspecified.
ASAD-NOTES:12:36#n35/r1.anchor: they were the King's cup-bearer and baker, both of them imprisoned for unspecified offences

ASAD-NOTES:12:36#n36/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:36#n36/r1.speaker: Baghawi, Zamakhshari, Baydawi
ASAD-NOTES:12:36#n36/r1.claim: These commentators take al-muhsinin here in the figurative sense of knowing something well, from ahsana.
ASAD-NOTES:12:36#n36/r1.anchor: This is the meaning given by Baghawi, Zamakhshari and Baydawi

ASAD-NOTES:12:36#n36/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:36#n36/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:36#n36/r2.claim: The elliptical passage indicates Joseph's reputation for wisdom and dream interpretation had reached the prison before him.
ASAD-NOTES:12:36#n36/r2.anchor: Joseph's reputation for wisdom and dream-interpretation preceded him to prison

STUDYQURAN:12:36/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r1.claim: Most commentaries identify the two young men as servants of Egypt’s king.
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r1.anchor: Most commentaries state that the two young men who were in prison with Joseph were servants to the king of Egypt.

STUDYQURAN:12:36/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r2.speaker: Ṭ and JJ
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r2.claim: One prisoner was the king’s baker and the other his wine carrier.
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r2.anchor: One of them was his baker (Ṭ) and the other his wine carrier (JJ, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:12:36/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r3.speaker: R and Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r3.claim: The baker had plotted to poison the king; the wine carrier was imprisoned as a suspected accomplice.
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r3.anchor: since the king thought that he had aided the baker in the attempt to kill him (R,Ṭ;

STUDYQURAN:12:36/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r4.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r4.claim: The wine dream belonged to the wine carrier, and the bread dream to the baker.
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r4.anchor: dreamed of the wine was the wine carrier, and the young man who had dreamed of the bread was the baker (Bg;

STUDYQURAN:12:36/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r5.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r5.claim: They asked Joseph to interpret their dreams because they had seen him interpret others’ dreams.
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r5.anchor: because they had seen him interpret other people’s dreams (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:12:36/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r6.speaker: Al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī says they trusted Joseph’s dream interpretation because his virtuous conduct, kindness, and devout practice showed him to be among the virtuous.
STUDYQURAN:12:36/r6.anchor: Al-Rāzī reports that, seeing Joseph’s virtuous character and kind behavior toward the other prison mates

TAB-FULL:v13p151/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p151/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p151/r1.claim: The account omits that Yusuf was first imprisoned; the youths' entry with him makes that missing event clear. They were servants of Egypt's senior king, one over drink and one over food.
TAB-FULL:v13p151/r1.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " فطرح في السجن، يعني يوسف، ودخل معه السجن فتيان، غلامان كانا للملك الأكبر

TAB-FULL:v13p151/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p151/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v13p151/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq names the king as al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid and the two servants as Mujlith and Nabu, with Nabu responsible for drink.
TAB-FULL:v13p151/r2.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " فطرح في السجن، يعني يوسف، ودخل معه السجن فتيان، غلامان كانا للملك الأكبر: الريان بن الوليد، كان أحدهما على شرابه

TAB-FULL:v13p151/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p151/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p151/r3.claim: Qatada identifies one youth as the king's baker and the other as his cupbearer.
TAB-FULL:v13p151/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، " {ودخل معه السجن فتيان} [يوسف: 36] قال: كان أحدهما خبازا للملك على طعامه، وكان الآخر ساقيه على شرابه

TAB-FULL:v13p151/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p151/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p151/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says the king jailed his baker for allegedly trying to poison him and jailed the cupbearer for suspected complicity.
TAB-FULL:v13p151/r4.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " إن الملك غضب على خبازه، بلغه أنه يريد أن يسمه، فحبسه وحبس صاحب شرابه

TAB-FULL:v13p153/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says Yusuf had announced he interpreted dreams, so the two youths pretended to have dreams to test his skill.
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r1.anchor: عن أسباط، عن السدي، قال: " لما دخل يوسف السجن قال: أنا أعبر الأحلام

TAB-FULL:v13p153/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r2.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says the two companions of Yusuf had seen nothing and only feigned dreams to test his knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: «ما رأى صاحبا يوسف شيئا، وإنما كانا تحالما ليجربا علمه»

TAB-FULL:v13p153/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq instead says they truly had dreams and admired Yusuf; Mujahid's account says Yusuf warned them that those who loved him had suffered trials, but they persisted in their affection.
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r3.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " لما رأى الفتيان يوسف، قالا: والله يا فتى لقد أحببناك حين رأيناك

TAB-FULL:v13p153/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r4.claim: Mujahid reports Yusuf asked them not to love him, recalling that his aunt, father, and the Aziz's wife had loved him and that each love brought him hardship.
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد " أن يوسف، قال لهم حين قالا له ذلك: أنشدكما الله أن لا تحباني

TAB-FULL:v13p153/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r5.claim: Aṣiru khamran means 'I see myself pressing grapes'; Ibn Masud's reading makes the intended object, grapes, explicit.
TAB-FULL:v13p153/r5.anchor: وعنى بقوله: {أعصر خمرا} [يوسف: 36] أي إني أرى في نومي أني أعصر عنبا

TAB-FULL:v13p155/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p155/r1.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
TAB-FULL:v13p155/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya reports Ibn Masud's reading as 'I see myself pressing grapes'; the passage says Omanis call grapes khamr.
TAB-FULL:v13p155/r1.anchor: عن محمد ابن الحنفية، قال " في قراءة ابن مسعود: «إني أراني أعصر عنبا»

TAB-FULL:v13p155/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p155/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v13p155/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak also explains khamr here as grapes, saying this is the usage of Oman and some other region.
TAB-FULL:v13p155/r2.anchor: قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: " {إني أراني أعصر خمرا} [يوسف: 36] يقول: أعصر عنبا، وهو بلغة أهل عمان

TAB-FULL:v13p155/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p155/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p155/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses khamr in this dream as grapes.
TAB-FULL:v13p155/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: " {إني أراني أعصر خمرا} [يوسف: 36] قال: عنبا

TAB-FULL:v13p155/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p155/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v13p155/r4.claim: Ikrima gives the dreamer's fuller vision: he planted a vine, pressed its grapes, served the king, and was told he would leave prison after three days to serve him wine.
TAB-FULL:v13p155/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: " أتاه فقال: رأيت فيما يرى النائم أني غرست حبلة من عنب، فنبتت، فخرج فيه عناقيد

TAB-FULL:v13p156/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p156/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p156/r1.claim: Ta'wil is what a matter ultimately leads or returns to; the youths ask Yusuf to tell them the outcome of what they saw in sleep.
TAB-FULL:v13p156/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، " {نبئنا بتأويله} [يوسف: 36] قال: به

TAB-FULL:v13p156/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p156/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p156/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as asking Yusuf to tell them about the dream itself; Abu Ubayd explains interpretation as the thing to which a matter leads.
TAB-FULL:v13p156/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، " {نبئنا بتأويله} [يوسف: 36] قال: به

TAB-FULL:v13p157/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p157/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v13p157/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak explains Yusuf's good conduct as tending the sick, helping the needy, and making room for those crowded in prison.
TAB-FULL:v13p157/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك بن مزاحم، قال: كنت جالسا معه ببلخ، فسئل عن قوله: " {نبئنا بتأويله إنا نراك من المحسنين} [يوسف: 36] قال: قيل له: ما كان إحسان يوسف؟ قال: كان إذا مرض إنسان قام عليه

TAB-FULL:v13p157/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p157/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p157/r2.claim: Qatada says Yusuf treated the sick, comforted the grieving, and strove in God's service; his encouragement gave despairing inmates patience and hope of reward.
TAB-FULL:v13p157/r2.anchor: عن أبي بكر بن عبد الله، عن قتادة، قوله: " {إنا نراك من المحسنين} [يوسف: 36] قال: بلغنا أن إحسانه أنه كان يداوي مريضهم، ويعزي حزينهم

TAB-FULL:v13p157/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p157/r3.speaker: يوسف
TAB-FULL:v13p157/r3.claim: In Qatada's account, Yusuf identified himself as son of Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham, while the prison keeper said he would give him the best confinement he could.
TAB-FULL:v13p157/r3.anchor: فمن أنت يا فتى؟ قال: أنا يوسف ابن صفي الله يعقوب ابن ذبيح الله إسحاق بن إبراهيم خليل الله

TAB-FULL:v13p159/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p159/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p159/r1.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the reports that Yusuf served inmates in practical ways. He answers that the youths call dream interpretation a kindness to them, like his other good deeds.
TAB-FULL:v13p159/r1.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك عندنا بالصواب القول الذي ذكرناه عن الضحاك وقتادة

TAB-FULL:v13p159/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p159/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p159/r2.claim: Although asking for a dream interpretation seems to praise knowledge, the phrase can mean: interpret it for us as a favor, just as you show goodness in your other actions.
TAB-FULL:v13p159/r2.anchor: نبئنا بتأويل رؤيانا محسنا إلينا في إخبارك إيانا بذلك، كما نراك تحسن في سائر أفعالك

TAB-FULL:v13p159/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p159/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v13p159/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq takes their praise of Yusuf as conditional: he would be one of the good-doers if he interpreted their dreams.
TAB-FULL:v13p159/r3.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " استفتياه في رؤياهما

TABATABAI:12:36-37/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r1.claim: The two fatayān were young male slaves; the context identifies them as servants of the king, as later reports will also say.
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r1.anchor: الفتى العبد وسياق الآيات يدل على أنهما كانا عبدين من عبيد الملك

TABATABAI:12:36-37/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r2.claim: The break before ‘one of them said’ separates the dreams from the entry into prison; arānī recounts a past dream, and squeezing wine means squeezing grapes intended for wine.
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r2.anchor: وقوله { أعصر خمرا } أي أعصر عنبا كما يعصر ليتخذ خمرا

TABATABAI:12:36-37/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r3.claim: The second prisoner dreamed of carrying bread that birds pecked from atop his head.
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r3.anchor: إني أرانى أحمل فوق رأسي خبزا تأكل الطير منه

TABATABAI:12:36-37/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r4.claim: The repeated ‘said’ replaces repeating the verb ‘tell us’; the pronoun in ‘its interpretation’ refers contextually to what each man saw in his dream.
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r4.anchor: فاكتفى عن ذكر الفعل بقوله { قال } { وقال } وهذا من لطائف تفنن القرآن

TABATABAI:12:36-37/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r5.claim: They believed Joseph was among the good because they saw signs of goodness in him, and thought good people’s pure hearts read events more soundly.
TABATABAI:12:36-37/r5.anchor: نعتقدك من المحسنين لما نشاهد فيك من سيماهم

TABATABAI:12:36-38/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:36-38/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:36-38/r2.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the dreams, so Joseph promises to interpret them before the food arrives; the author finds this less likely in context.
TABATABAI:12:36-38/r2.anchor: وأما على تقدير عود ضمير { بتأويله } إلى ما رأياه من الرؤيا

TABATABAI:12:41-42#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:41-42#2/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:41-42#2/r2.claim: The same report identifies the two young men as the king’s servants, a baker and a cupbearer, and says the baker had fabricated the dream and was the one crucified.
TABATABAI:12:41-42#2/r2.anchor: ودخل معه السجن فتيان يقول عبدان للملك أحدهما خباز والآخر صاحب الشراب

TABATABAI:12:41-42#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:41-42#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:41-42#2/r3.claim: Joseph was called a benefactor because he cared for the sick, sought help for the needy, and treated fellow prisoners generously.
TABATABAI:12:41-42#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله

TABATABAI:12:83-92#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:83-92#3/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:83-92#3/r5.claim: Joseph's excellence included making room for people, borrowing for the needy, and helping the weak.
TABATABAI:12:83-92#3/r5.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل { إنا نراك من المحسنين } قال

TABATABAI:12:93-102#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#13/r2.claim: The Qur'an also recounts Joseph's dream, his prison companions' dreams, and Pharaoh's dream.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#13/r2.anchor: ومنها ما حكاه تعالى من رؤيا يوسف عليه السلام إذ قال يوسف لأبيه يا أبت إني رأيت

TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r1.claim: Everyone has encountered dreams that reveal hidden matters or future events, especially clear dreams requiring no interpretation; their correspondence to later events cannot be dismissed as coincidence.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r1.anchor: ما منا واحد إلا وقد شاهد من نفسه شيئا من الرؤى والمنامات دله على بعض الأمور الخفية

TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r2.claim: Dreaming is a mental act involving imagination, which recombines stored sensory images; bodily conditions, temperament, and emotions shape many ordinary dreams.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r2.anchor: والمتخيلة من القوى الفعالة دائما ربما تدوم في عملها من جهة الأنباء الواردة عليها من ناحية الحس

TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r3.claim: Naturalist critics correctly identify bodily and emotional causes that shape many dreams, but their account only shows that some dreams lack truth.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r3.anchor: وهذا هو الذي ذكره منكروا حقيقة الرؤيا من علماء الطبيعة لا يزيد على تعداد هذه الأسباب

TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r4.claim: The claim that every dream is unreal does not follow: some sound dreams reveal truths and have a real relation to external events.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r4.anchor: وهو غير المدعى وهو أن كل منام ليس ذا حقيقة فإن هناك منامات صالحة ورؤيا صادقة

TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r1.claim: Every dream has causes and thus an interpretation, but causes vary: bodily or temperamental influences, chance circumstances, and preoccupations can produce dreams without foretelling external events.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r1.anchor: فقد ظهر مما بينا أن جميع الرؤى لا تخلو عن حقيقة بمعنى أن هذه الإدراكات المتنوعة المختلفة

TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r2.claim: The relevant true dreams are those not caused by external bodily or accidental factors, nor internal dispositions, yet connected to external events and cosmic realities.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r2.anchor: وإنما البحث في نوع واحد من هذه المنامات

TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r3.claim: Because future or hidden events are absent from the dreamer's senses, the author proposes that the sleeping soul connects to their causes beyond the physical world.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r3.anchor: ولذا قيل إن الارتباط إنما استقر بينها وبين النفس النائمة من جهة اتصال النفس بسبب الحادثة الواقعة

TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r4.claim: He distinguishes the physical world of changing matter, the imaginal world of immaterial forms that causes physical events, and the intellectual world of universal truths that causes the imaginal realm.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r4.anchor: أن العوالم ثلاثة عالم الطبيعة وهو العالم الدنيوي الذي نعيش فيه والأشياء الموجودة فيها صور مادية

TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r1.claim: A soul able to grasp intellectual realities may see universal causes directly; otherwise it represents them through familiar images, and a sound soul may perceive causes without alteration in a clear dream.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r1.anchor: فإن كانت النفس كاملة متمكنة من إدراك المجردات العقلية أدركتها واستحضرت أسباب الكائنات

TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r2.claim: Other true dreams use symbols or opposites, such as a crown for honor or darkness for ignorance; these require interpretation by returning each image to the reality first perceived.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r2.anchor: وهذه هي التي تحتاج إلى التعبير بردها إلى الأصل الذي هو المشهود الأولى للنفس كرد التاج إلى الفخار

TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r3.claim: Symbolic dreams divide into manageable transformations and tangled sequences of transformations; the latter are confused dreams that resist interpretation, unlike clear dreams and interpretable symbolic dreams.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r3.anchor: المنامات التي تصرفت فيها النفس بالحكاية والتمثيل

TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r4.speaker: ابن سيرين
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r4.claim: In an example, Ibn Sīrīn interprets a dream of sealing people's mouths and sexual organs with a ring as becoming a Ramadan caller whose adhān makes people fast.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r4.anchor: أن رجلا رأى في المنام أن بيده خاتما يختم به أفواه الناس وفروجهم فسأل ابن سيرين

TABRISI:12:36-38/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:36-38/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:36-38/r1.claim: The citation to call people to God's path with wisdom frames the account of Yusuf's religious address to the prisoners.
TABRISI:12:36-38/r1.anchor: ادع إلى سبيل ربك بالحكمة والموعظة الحسنة

TABRISI:12:36-38/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:36-38/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:36-38/r2.claim: The two prisoners said they had come to love Yusuf; he replied that affection for him had repeatedly brought him hardship: his aunt's love led to a theft accusation, his father's to the well, and the Aziz's wife's to prison.
TABRISI:12:36-38/r2.anchor: لا تحباني فوالله ما أحبني أحد إلا دخل علي من حبه بلاء

THALABI:v5p221/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p221/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p221/r1.claim: The two prison newcomers were servants of King al-Akbar al-Walid ibn al-Rayyan: baker Majlath and cupbearer Banu; the king imprisoned them over an alleged poisoning plot.
THALABI:v5p221/r1.anchor: وهما غلامان كانا للملك الأكبر الوليد بن الريان، أحدهما خبازه صاحب طعامه

THALABI:v5p221/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p221/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p221/r2.claim: The account says Egyptians bribed the two servants to poison the king’s food and drink; the cupbearer backed out, but the baker accepted the bribe and poisoned the food.
THALABI:v5p221/r2.anchor: ضمنوا لهما مالا ليسما طعام الملك وشرابه فأجاباهم إلى ذلك

THALABI:v5p222/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p222/r1.claim: The cupbearer warned the king not to eat, the baker warned him not to drink, and a test on an animal showed the food was poisoned, so both men were jailed.
THALABI:v5p222/r1.anchor: فقال الملك للساقي: اشرب فشربه فلم يضره، وقال للخباز: كل من طعامك

THALABI:v5p222/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p222/r2.claim: Joseph had told prisoners he could interpret dreams; the two men approached to test him even though, Ibn Masʿud says, they had not actually dreamed anything.
THALABI:v5p222/r2.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: ما رأى صاحبا يوسف شيئا، إنما كانا تحالفا أن يجربا علمه

THALABI:v5p222/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222/r3.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p222/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits a prophetic warning that whoever falsely claims to have seen a dream will be ordered to tie two barley grains together on Judgment Day.
THALABI:v5p222/r3.anchor: من أرى عينيه في المنام ما لم تريا كلف أن يعقد بين شعرتين يوم القيامة

THALABI:v5p222/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222/r4.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p222/r4.claim: The same report warns that secretly listening to people who dislike it brings molten lead poured into the listener’s ear.
THALABI:v5p222/r4.anchor: ومن استمع لحديث قوم وهم له كارهون صب في أذنه الآنك

THALABI:v5p222/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222/r5.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v5p222/r5.claim: Mujahid says the two men loved Joseph at first sight; Joseph warned that those who loved him had each suffered a calamity, including his aunt, father, and the king’s wife.
THALABI:v5p222/r5.anchor: قال مجاهد: لما رأى الفتيان يوسف قالا له: والله لقد أحببناك

THALABI:v5p222/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v5p222/r6.claim: The cupbearer’s dream showed a grape seed bearing three clusters which he squeezed into the king’s cup and served him.
THALABI:v5p222/r6.anchor: فقال له الساقي: أيها العالم إني رأيت كأني غرست حبة من عنب

THALABI:v5p222/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222/r7.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v5p222/r7.claim: The baker’s dream showed three baskets of food above his head, eaten by birds; Ibn Masʿud’s reading clarifies the grape image as pressing grapes.
THALABI:v5p222/r7.anchor: وقال الخباز: إني رأيت كأن فوق رأسي ثلاث سلال فيها الخبز

THALABI:v5p222/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v5p222/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads the cupbearer as saying he pressed grapes, making explicit that the word khamr here means grapes.
THALABI:v5p222/r8.anchor: ويدل عليه قراءة ابن مسعود أعصر عنبا

THALABI:v5p222#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222#2/r1.speaker: الأصمعي
THALABI:v5p222#2/r1.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says an Arab called grapes he carried khamr, and vinegar made from grapes was also called wine-vinegar by association.
THALABI:v5p222#2/r1.anchor: قال الأصمعي: أخبرني المعتمر أنه لقي أعرابيا معه عنب، فقال: ما معك؟ قال: خمر

THALABI:v5p222#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222#2/r2.speaker: القتيبي
THALABI:v5p222#2/r2.claim: Al-Qutaybi allows literal wine by analogy with saying one pressed oil when olives were pressed.
THALABI:v5p222#2/r2.anchor: قال القتيبي: وقد تكون هي الخمر بعينها كما يقال: عصرت زيتا

THALABI:v5p222#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222#2/r3.speaker: الفراء وابن إسحاق
THALABI:v5p222#2/r3.claim: Al-Farra and Ibn Ishaq say the prisoners call Joseph beneficent to them if he interprets their dreams; the phrase can be a polite appeal.
THALABI:v5p222#2/r3.anchor: قال الفراء وقال ابن إسحاق: إنا نراك من المحسنين إلينا إن فعلت ذلك

THALABI:v5p222#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v5p222#2/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says Joseph’s kindness in prison meant visiting the sick, making room for the cramped, gathering aid for the needy, and interceding for them.
THALABI:v5p222#2/r4.anchor: في قوله: إنا نراك من المحسنين ما كان إحسانه؟ قال كان إذا مرض رجل

THALABI:v5p222#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v5p222#2/r5.claim: Qatada says Joseph treated sick prisoners, comforted the grieving, and devoted himself to his Lord.
THALABI:v5p222#2/r5.anchor: قتادة: بلغنا أن إحسانه كان يداوي مريضهم، ويعزي حزينهم

THALABI:v5p222#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p222#2/r6.claim: Another story says Joseph encouraged hopeless inmates with promises of reward and cleansing; his kindness made the jailer let him choose any cell.
THALABI:v5p222#2/r6.anchor: فجعل يقول: أبشروا واصبروا تؤجروا، وإن لهذا لأجرا وثوابا

THALABI:v5p222#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p222#2/r7.claim: Joseph avoided immediately interpreting the dream because he knew one prisoner would suffer, and instead changed the subject.
THALABI:v5p222#2/r7.anchor: فكره يوسف (عليه السلام) أن يعبر لهما ما سألاه لما علم في ذلك من المكروه على أحدهما

THALABI:v5p222#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p222#2/r8.claim: Most commentators understand Joseph’s promise to explain their food dreams before the food arrives as a claim to prophetic foreknowledge.

THALABI:v5p222#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p222#2/r9.claim: Another view says he meant their ordinary waking food, telling them what it was, when they ate, and how much; they suspected divination, but he attributed knowledge to God.
THALABI:v5p222#2/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم: أراد به في اليقظة فقال: لا يأتيكما طعام ترزقانه تطعمانه وتأكلانه

THALABI:v5p222#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p222#2/r10.claim: The repeated phrase that they are disbelievers in the Hereafter is analyzed as emphasis; another grammatical view treats the first pronoun as redundant and the second clause as the sentence.
THALABI:v5p222#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: هم الأول جماد كقوله تعالى: أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم

THALABI:v5p222#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p222#2/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p222#2/r11.claim: The text compares the grammatical redundancy with a Quranic construction in which the first clause is treated as omitted and the next begins anew.
THALABI:v5p222#2/r11.anchor: فصارت الأولى الملغاة والثانية ابتداء، وكافرون خبره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r1.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r1.claim: The two young men were servants of Egypt's king, one over his food and one over his drink; the food steward was suspected of plotting to poison the king, and both were jailed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r1.anchor: قال السدي (¬6) وقتادة (¬7) والمفسرون (¬8): هما غلامان كانا لملك مصر الأكبر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r2.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r2.claim: Qatāda shares the account that the king's food and drink stewards were jailed after suspicion of a poisoning plot.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r2.anchor: قال السدي (¬6) وقتادة (¬7) والمفسرون (¬8): هما غلامان كانا لملك مصر الأكبر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r3.claim: فتى can mean a strong young man, but the two could have been young or old because enslaved people were called فتًى; “entered with him” implies Joseph was imprisoned too.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬2): ويجوز أن يكونا حدثين أو شيخين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r4.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, the two were the king's servants, one assigned to drink and the other to food.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬3) في رواية عطاء: في قوله (فتيان) عبدان للملك، وكان أحدهما على شراب الملك،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r5.claim: Joseph told the prison inmates he interpreted dreams; the two men asked him to test his skill although they had not actually dreamed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬4) كان يوسف لما دخل السجن قال لأهله: إني أعبر الأحلام،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the prisoners had no dreams; they pretended to have dreamed to test Joseph's knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r6.anchor: قال ابن مسعود (¬5): ما رأيا شيئا، إنما كانا تحالما ليجربا علمه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r7.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r7.claim: Mujāhid says they really had dreams upon entering prison; the cupbearer dreamed of a vine with three branches and serving its grapes as wine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد (¬6): كانا قد رأيا حين أدخل السجن رؤيا، فأتيا يوسف، فقال له الساقي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r8.claim: The wording need not say “I saw myself in a dream,” because context shows he was not awake pressing wine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r8.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬1): لم يقل إني أراني في النوم أعصر خمرا، لأن الحال يدل على أنه ليس يرى نفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r9.claim: Without intending a dream, أعصر would suffice; أراني would be unnecessary.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r9.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: لأنه لو لم يقصد للنوم كان قوله (أعصر) مستغنى به عن {أراني}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r10.claim: Another argument that the men dreamed is their request for an interpretation, since waking experience does not require interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p111/r10.anchor: وقال غيرهما: قد دل على المنام قولهما {نبئنا بتأويله} وذلك أنه لا يكون لما يرى في اليقظة تأويل.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r1.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r1.claim: عصرت means personally squeezing grapes, اعتصرت means having someone squeeze them for you, and العصارة is the liquid expressed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r1.anchor: قال الليث (¬2): يقال: عصرت العنب وعصرته، إذا وليت عصره بنفسك، واعتصرت إذا عصر لك،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r2.claim: One reading of أعصر خمرا supplies an omitted noun: Joseph presses grapes intended to become wine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r2.anchor: وذكر المفسرون (¬3) وأهل المعاني في قوله: {أعصر خمرا} ثلاثة أقوال: أحدها: أن يكون المعنى أعصر عنب خمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r3.claim: Another reading names a thing by what it will become, as speakers say they cook bricks when they mean clay, or cook molasses or juice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r3.anchor: والثاني: أن العرب تسمي الشيء باسم ما يؤول إليه إذا انكشف المعنى ولم يلتبس،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī agrees that the expression can name grapes by their eventual product, wine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r4.anchor: هذا (¬4) الذي ذكرنا قول الزجاج (¬5) وابن الأنباري (¬6).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r5.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the Quran was revealed in the languages of different peoples; some called grapes wine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r5.anchor: قال الضحاك (¬1): نزل القرآن بكل لسان، والعنب بلغة بعضهم الخمر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r6.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r6.claim: Al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, reports that the tribes of Azd and Oman called grapes wine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r6.anchor: وقال الكلبي عن أبي صالح (¬2): أزد وعمان يسمون العنب الخمر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r7.speaker: الأصمعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r7.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī relates that al-Muʿtamir asked a Bedouin carrying grapes what he had, and the man answered “wine.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r7.anchor: وحكى الأصمعي (¬3) عن المعتمر أنه لقي أعرابيا معه عنب، فقال: ما معك؟ قال: خمر (¬4).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r8.claim: The food steward dreamed of baskets of bread and food on his head while birds pecked at them, corresponding to the verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r8.anchor: وقال صاحب الطعام (ليوسف: إني رأيت) (¬5) كأن فوق رأسي ثلاث سلال فيها الخبز وألوان الأطعمة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r9.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r9.claim: الطير is a feminine collective noun; its singular is طائر.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r9.anchor: (وقال الليث (¬7): الطير اسم جامع) (¬8) مؤنث، والواحد طائر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r10.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r10.claim: Aḥmad b. Yaḥyā says people use طائر for one bird; Abū ʿUbayda agrees, then uniquely permits طير as singular with plural طيور.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p113/r10.anchor: وقال أحمد بن يحيى (¬9): الناس كلهم يقولون للواحد طائر، # وأبو عبيدة (¬1) معهم،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r1.claim: تأويل means interpretation; Abū ʿUbayd defines a thing's interpretation as its eventual return or outcome.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬2): أخبرنا بتفسيره، قال أبو عبيد (¬3): تأويل الشيء ما يرجع إليه وتصرف من المعنى الذي تحته.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r2.claim: Joseph was counted among the virtuous because he cared for sick inmates, comforted the grieving, and maintained obedience to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r2.anchor: ما قاله إبراهيم وقتادة (¬5): كان يعود مرضاهم، ويعزي حزينهم، ورأوا منه محافظة على طاعة الله عز وجل فأحبوه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r3.claim: Qatāda shares the report that Joseph visited the sick, comforted the grieving, and obeyed God, winning the inmates' affection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r3.anchor: ما قاله إبراهيم وقتادة (¬5): كان يعود مرضاهم، ويعزي حزينهم، ورأوا منه محافظة على طاعة الله عز وجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r4.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Joseph attended the sick, made room for the cramped, and gathered aid for anyone in need.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r4.anchor: قال (¬6) الضحاك (¬7): كان إذا مرض رجل في السجن قام عليه، وإذا ضاق وسع له، وإن احتاج جمع له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r5.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reads “you are among the good” as a promise of gratitude if Joseph interprets the two dreams for them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r5.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن إسحاق (¬8): قال: إنا نراك من المحسنين إن فسرت لنا هذين المنامين.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ interprets المحسنين as knowledgeable; Ibn al-Anbārī supplies “in knowledge,” and al-Zajjāj says skilled at interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r6.anchor: وقال الفراء (¬1): إنا نراك من المحسنين، يقول من العالمين قد أحسنت العلم،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r7.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj says this verse proves dreams can be true and occurred among earlier peoples; denying that any dream comes true rejects scripture and reports.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r7.anchor: نحو هذا قال الزجاج (¬3): أي ممن يحسن التأويل (¬4)، قال: وهذا دليل أن أمر الرؤيا صحيح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r8.claim: God's grace made Joseph's interpretive skill and kindness the means of his eventual release, since explaining the dreams led to his rescue.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p115/r8.anchor: وهذه الآية بيان عما يوجبه لطف الله تعالى فيما سببه لنجاة يوسف بالعلم والإحسان في جوابه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r4.claim: The two young men were servants to the king: the food servant was accused of poisoning him, and the drink servant of conspiring with him, so both were jailed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r4.anchor: رفع إليه أن صاحب طعامه يريد أن يسمه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r5.claim: They tested Joseph by inventing dreams rather than actually seeing them; the cupbearer dreamed of pressing grapes into wine, and the food servant of birds eating bread above his head.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r5.anchor: وهو الساقي { إني أراني أعصر خمرا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r6.claim: The food servant's dream showed birds of prey pecking at the bread on his head; they asked Joseph to interpret it because they saw him as a benefactor.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r7.claim: Before answering, Joseph diverted from their question and first let them know he could interpret dreams.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r7.anchor: ودلهما أولا على أنه عالم بتفسير الرؤيا

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:36/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:36/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:36/r1.claim: Tafsir reports say the king’s cupbearer and baker were jailed after conspirators trying to kill the king prompted them to poison his drink and bread; each then accused the other.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:36/r1.anchor: Tefsirlerdeki rivayetlere göre bu iki genç, Mısır’da kralı öldürmek isteyen kimselerin teşvikiyle onun ekmeğine ve şarabına zehir katmışlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:36/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:36/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:36/r2.claim: One dreamed of squeezing grapes for wine and the other of carrying bread while a bird ate from it; unable to interpret the dreams, they asked Joseph, whose truthfulness, knowledge, interpretation, and character they trusted.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:36/r2.anchor: Bunun üzerine her ikisi de doğruluğuna, ilmine, yorumuna ve şahsiyetine güvendikleri Yûsuf’a gelip ondan rüyalarının yorumunu istediler

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Two inmates’ dreams and Joseph’s correct interpretations ultimately create the opportunity for him to interpret the reigning king’s dream, after which the king entrusts him with control of the kingdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: He does so and the interpretation proves to be absolutely true. Ultimately, this paves the way of he interpreting the dream seen by the reigning king.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur'an leaves the two prisoners unidentified.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The Qur’ ān has not revealed the identity of the two young boys.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: Torah
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: On the Torah's account, one youth served the king wine and the other was his baker.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Torah is accepted, it seems that one of them had the duty to serve wine to the king and the other one was his baker.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Their unusual dreams made them curious, and having observed Joseph's knowledge and piety, they naturally asked him to interpret them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: were impressed by his knowledge and piety. Thus it was very natural that they termed to him for this interpretation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Muhsin describes someone who acts in everything as if standing in God's presence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: someone who does everything as if he is standing in God’s presence.

TABATABAI:12:6#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:6#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:6#2/r1.claim: Dream interpretation appears in Jacob’s explanation of Joseph’s dream, Joseph’s interpretation of his own, his companions’ and the king’s dreams, and in waking predictions taught by God.
TABATABAI:12:6#2/r1.anchor: ما حكاه الله تعالى من بيان يعقوب تأويل رؤيا يوسف عليه السلام
